text: My message is that we'll be watching you.
note: Personal testimony, direct address and warning

text: This is all wrong.
note: General statement of disapproval

text: I shouldn't be up here.
note: Speaker's personal situation

text: I should be back in school on the other side of the ocean.
note: Personal testimony about her rightful place

text: Yet you all come to us young people for hope.
note: Contrast between her situation and leaders' actions

text: How dare you?
note: Rhetorical question, direct accusation

text: You have stolen my dreams and my childhood with your empty words.
note: Direct accusation of personal loss

text: And yet I'm one of the lucky ones.
note: Contrast, setting up the next list

text: People are suffering.
note: First item in a list of three

text: People are dying.
note: Second item in a list of three, anaphora

text: entire ecosystems are collapsing.
note: Third item in a list of three

text: We are in the beginning of a mass extinction, and all you can talk about is money and fairy tales of eternal economic growth.
note: Warning, contrast between reality and leaders' focus

text: How dare you?
note: Repetition of 'How dare you?'

text: For more than 30 years, the science has been crystal clear.
note: Statistic, factual statement

text: How dare you continue to look away and come here saying that you're doing enough when the politics and solutions needed are still nowhere in sight.
note: Third 'How dare you?', direct accusation of inaction and deception

text: You say you hear us and that you understand the urgency.
note: Direct address, setting up a contrast

text: But no matter how sad and angry I am, I do not want to believe that.
note: Personal testimony, contrast of emotion and belief

text: Because if you really understood the situation and still kept on failing to act,
note: Conditional accusation

text: then you would be evil, and that I refuse to believe.
note: Completes the conditional accusation, personal testimony

text: The popular idea of cutting our emissions in half in 10 years only gives us a 50% chance of staying below 1.5 degrees and the risk of setting off irreversible chain reactions beyond human control.
note: Statistics and warning

text: 50% may be acceptable to you.
note: Statistic, direct address, setting up a contrast

text: But those numbers do not include tipping points, most feedback loops, additional warming hidden by toxic air pollution or the aspects of equity and climate justice.
note: Contrast, explaining flaws in statistics

text: They also rely on my generation sucking hundreds of billions of tons of your CO2 out of the air with technologies that barely exist.
note: Accusation, statistic, personal stakes

text: So a 50% risk is simply not acceptable to us.
note: Statistic, defiance, contrast to previous statement

text: we who have to live with the consequences.
note: Clarification of 'us'

text: To have a 67% chance of staying below a 1.5 degrees of global temperature rise, the best odds given by the IPCC, the world had 420 gigatons of CO2 left to emit back on January 1st, 2018.
note: Scientific statistics and dates

text: Today, that figure is already down to less than 350 gigatons.
note: Updated statistic, implicit contrast

text: How dare you pretend that this can be sold with just business as usual and some technical solutions?
note: Fourth 'How dare you?', direct accusation of deception

text: With today's emissions levels, that remaining CO2 budget will be entirely gone within less than eight and a half years.
note: Statistic, warning about timeline

text: There will not be any solutions or plans presented in line with these figures here today because these numbers are too uncomfortable
note: Prediction of inaction, accusation of discomfort

text: And you are still not mature enough to tell it like it is.
note: Direct accusation of immaturity and dishonesty

text: You are failing us.
note: Direct and concise accusation

text: But the young people are starting to understand your betrayal.
note: Contrast, accusation of betrayal

text: The eyes of all future generations are upon you.
note: Direct address, warning of future judgment

text: And if you choose to fail us, I say we will never forgive you.
note: Conditional warning, direct address, personal testimony

text: We will not let you get away with this.
note: Direct address, warning, defiance

text: Right here, right now is where we draw the line.
note: Powerful statement of resolve, punchline

text: The world is waking up and change is coming whether you like it or not.
note: Punchline, warning, statement of inevitable change

text: Thank you.
note: Standard closing
